note: DOWNHILL — Urban FPV (https://downhill-eta.vercel.app/) is capture-class: a hand-written ES module graph served at the origin root by a Vercel static deploy (no bundler in the app layer; only the two three.js r183 builds are minified vendor code). §0.4 fork-over-mirror was checked on 2026-10-13 — src/main.js credits the author Sree Menon and links https://github.com/msreekm/downhill as the "GitHub repo", but that repository answers 404 (removed or never public): no public source exists, so the mirror stands (recorded in README.md §0.4). Derived pipeline: capture → pinned prettier 3.9.6 (module API, default options, single pass verified idempotent — never the CLI: it respects .gitignore and can silently echo its input) → readable/<name>.pretty.js per captured JS file (capture-relative name, nested dirs flattened with __; every pretty provably NOT byte-identical to its capture source) → statement-aligned slices src/<name>-NN.js of every APP module (top-level declaration boundaries only, ~250-350 line windows; oversized single declarations stay whole) with an exact 2-line provenance header. Every slice parses standalone under `node --input-type=module --check -` and round-trips byte-exact to its recorded readable line range. Layout divergence (README): the origin serves the app under /src/ and the vendored libraries under /vendor/, so the byte-exact capture lives at src/*.js and vendor/** at the repo root — derived slices share src/ with the captured modules and are never listed in .upstream/manifest.json. Vendor rule — wholeFile sections, never sliced: the three.js r183 builds (three.module.min.js imports three.core.min.js) and the BufferGeometryUtils addon. Stylesheet rule: src/style.css is wholeFile. Inline scan: index.html carries an inline importmap — twin readable/index-inline-1.pretty.json + readable/index-inline-map.json with byte range + sha256. Non-standalone parts are indexed but never sliced (skipped sections): a pure trailing export {…} table where one exists — this capture's app layer has none. Identifiers in src/ are the app's own declared names — no rename campaign applies (PLAN §5) since the served code is not minified. Capture bytes are untouched by everything above; re-cut with `node tools/derive.mjs` after any capture refresh. `node tools/audit.js` is the gate.
coverageNote: Export-name gate coverage (tools/check-exports.mjs; measured 2026-10-27). The capture carries 67 ES export tables: 63 across the sixteen app modules, 4 across the three vendored three.js files. 63 are CHECKED against derived text that is a DIFFERENT file — for every app module the pristine is its prettier reading copy under readable/ and the derived text is its statement-aligned src/src__<module>-NN.js slice, so renaming a public name on either side turns the gate red and names the file and the binding. 4 are NOT covered, and that is the honest outcome: vendor/three.module.min.js (2 tables, 243 + 197 public names), vendor/three.core.min.js (1 table, 442 names) and vendor/BufferGeometryUtils.js (1 table, 13 names). The vendor rule (PLAN §1) ships these files byte-exact and renders each whole to readable/vendor__<name>.pretty.js, never sliced: the reading copy IS the layer's terminal text, so the gate has no derived text downstream of it to compare, and comparing it with itself is exactly the self-compare the gate refuses. Naming the served capture a second time does not reach them — it counts the same table twice and doubles the NOT-covered line (measured 4 → 8 in a throwaway copy), so it is not done: one table, one name. Importer evidence that all four are load-bearing: index.html's import map maps `three` → /vendor/three.module.min.js and `three/addons/utils/BufferGeometryUtils.js` → /vendor/BufferGeometryUtils.js; eight app modules import * as THREE from `three`; src/world.js imports mergeGeometries from the addon; and vendor/three.module.min.js imports ./three.core.min.js. Their bytes — and so every public name in them — stay pinned by tools/verify.mjs against .upstream/manifest.json, and tools/audit.js resolves all 42 imports (including the 2 import-map entries) against the capture and keeps the vendor sections' content guards. No mapping to a DISTINCT derived file is recorded: the only spec-only shape that would raise checked to 67 points a wholeFile section's `file` at the served capture instead of at a derived slice, which silently disables audit.js's vendor content guard and would be reverted by tools/derive.mjs --check, so it is not written.
